Click a cell to toggle it. Drag to paint; a drag that starts on a live cell erases. Right-drag always erases.

Each cell under the brush is decided once per stroke, so the density you set is the density you get.

Competition

A cell converts when at least this many neighbors belong to the species that beats it. The neighborhood setting under Rules applies here too.

Fill and edit
Still lifes, oscillators, spaceships
Active0
Still0
Oscillating 0
Moving 0

Each cell is judged by its own recent history: alive for 8 straight generations counts as still; a repeating on/off rhythm of period 2 to 15 counts as oscillating; a cell whose whole neighborhood repeats an earlier state shifted up to two cells over (period 2 to 12) counts as moving, which picks out gliders and other spaceships. Newly edited cells need a few dozen generations before they are classified. Hidden cells still take part in the simulation.

Cell shape
Rules

Rock-paper-scissors mode does not use a Life rule. Its settings are under Competition.

Neighborhood

B lists the neighbor counts that bring a dead cell to life. S lists the counts that keep a live cell alive. C (Generations rules) is the number of states: a cell that fails to survive fades through C−2 dying states that cannot be reborn or count as neighbors.

Import and export

RLE is the format used by the LifeWiki, Golly and Catagolue. Pasted stamps and copied regions are kept in this browser under “Your stamps”.

John Conway devised Life in 1970, and Martin Gardner introduced it in his Mathematical Games column in Scientific American that October. Conway first worked patterns out by hand with stones on a Go board; switch Cell shape to Go stone to play it that way. Reset returns to the board as it was when you last pressed Play or Step after editing.

Point at a cell to see its neighbor count.
